newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease on Yeltsin, US bond fears.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease on Yeltsin, US bond fears.

text.p: Russian MinFin bond prices eased from earlier levels on a fall in U.S. Treasuries after news of a strong increase in U.S. payrolls in December, and on concerns about President Boris Yeltsin's health, dealers said.
U.S. Treasuries fell on the December jobs report, on fears of a U.S. rate hike.
A top Kremlin doctor said on Friday Yeltsin, suffering from pneumonia, will spend at least another three days in hospital and then will need a three-week rehabilitation period.
"The market was rising in the morning but the decline started ahead of the U.S. payrolls and is continuing now," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.
Dealers said the most liquid third, fourth and fifth tranches were finding support at 83.00, 59.00 and 41.00 respectively but they found it difficult to forecast for how long.

"The market is facing a double blow from fears about Yeltsin and U.S. Treasuries. Investors are not willing to keep MinFins over the weekend so the trend is on the downside," Bankers Trust dealer Adam Elstein said.
